_meta.description: The environment a capture has to come from for the fixture to mean anything. Recorded into every captured fixture by tools/evtx_to_fixture.py.
_meta.why: A captured event is evidence about one specific machine: this Windows build, this Sysmon version, this configuration. Without that recorded, 'captured' means 'someone once saw this on some box' - a claim that cannot be re-run and cannot be argued with when a rule stops firing.
_meta.honest_limit: No VM image has been built from this manifest. It describes the intended lab host, and a capture records which of these values the box it came from actually reported. The values are checked for shape and internal consistency, not against a machine that exists. G-21 stays partly open for that reason: this makes a capture attestable, it does not create the reproducible image.

os.note: Not Windows Server: the proxy and EDR telemetry in this lab exists on a workstation, and Sysmon's default behaviour differs by SKU in the areas the persistence rules read.

sysmon.note: The config hash is recorded per fixture; the version is recorded here because a schema change silently drops fields a rule reads.

required_audit_policy.note: Security 4663 does not exist without a SACL. A 4663-based rule on a host without this audits nothing and never fires - the same silent failure as a missing field alias.

clock.note: Fixtures carry _utc; a capture from a host in local time produces sequence fixtures that order wrongly. This is the defect that made the earlier sequence fixture unevaluatable.
